data.name: Badran
data.gender_notes: Badran is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Badr' meaning 'moon'. Badran is a name of honor and strength, reminiscent of warriors and riders in Islamic history. The name Badran carries the meaning “Rider, Warrior” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Badran usually hope their child will grow to embody rider, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Badran is deeply spiritual and represents the fullness of life. It is a reminder of the cycle of life and the importance of embracing the natural world. It is a name that is often given to boys who are strong, courageous, and full of potential.
data.etymology: Badran belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rider, Warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Badran total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: بدران
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من بدر، يعني كمال أو تمام في الإسلام
in_arabic.long_meaning: بدران هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: كامل، مكتمل، أو تمام. وهو مشتق من اسم بدر الذي يشير إلى القمر في تمام نوره، ويرتبط بالكمال والتمام في الإسلام. وقد ورد ذكر اسم بدر في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران: «وَدَعَوا زُلَيْخَةَ تَطَلُبُ مِنَ الْمَلِكِ إِذْ أَظلَمَ وَقَالَتْ يَا سَيِّدِيَ السِّجْنَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعونَنِي إِلَيْهِ وَإِنْ لَمْ تَصْفَحُوا عَنِّي رِشحاً أَسْعَدى السَّجْنَ وَأَلذ لِذاكِ وَأَنا بِالآخِرَةِ مُؤْمِنٌ وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ رَبِّي إِنَّ رَبِّيَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ»

in_urdu.name: بدران
in_urdu.meaning: کمال یا تمام کے معنی میں اسلامی نام
in_urdu.long_meaning: بدران ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہے مکمل، کامل یا تمام۔ یہ نام بدر سے مشتق ہے جو چاند کے پورے ہونے کے معنی میں ہے اور اسلامی تقویم میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لئے، یہ نام روحانی اہمیت کا حامل ہے کیونکہ یہ کمال اور مثالیں کی تجلی کا اظہار کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बदरान
in_hindi.meaning: इस्लामी नाम, पूर्णता या सम्पूर्णता के अर्थ में
in_hindi.long_meaning: बदरान एक मस्कुलिन नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से निकला है और इसका अर्थ है पूर्ण, सम्पूर्ण या पूरा। यह नाम बद्र से व्युत्पन्न है, जो चंद्रमा के पूर्ण होने के अर्थ में है और इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्व रखता है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम आध्यात्मिक महत्व का वाहक है क्योंकि यह पूर्णता और आदर्शों की अभिव्यक्ति को दर्शाता है।

in_english.name: Badran
in_english.meaning: Islamic name meaning full, complete, or perfect
in_english.long_meaning: Badran is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning full, complete, or perfect. Etymologically derived from 'badr', which refers to the full moon, the name symbolizes completeness and perfection. In Islamic tradition, the name is associated with positive attributes such as spiritual maturity and ideal character. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting its significance in Islamic heritage. The name Badran is also linked to Quranic references that emphasize the themes of completion and divine guidance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Badran is deeply rooted in Islamic history, as it is the name of a prince from the Banu Bakr, a noble tribe in ancient Arabia prior to the advent of Islam. He was part of the Battle of Badr, a significant military engagement between the Prophet Muhammad's forces and those of the Meccan Quraysh in 624 AD. The importance of this battle lies in its early strategic victory for the Muslims, as it marked their first large-scale battle and was a turning point in the spread of the early Islamic community. The name Badran was reportedly given to honor the warriors who took part in this battle.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Badran, meaning 'moon', holds spiritual significance as the moon is often described as a symbol of divine guidance in Islamic traditions. In Surah Al-An'am (6:97), Allah says, "It is He Who makes the stars for you, so that you may be guided in the darkness of the land and sea." The moon, as a source of light and guidance, is an essential element in Islamic cosmology. Thus, the name Badran is a reminder of the protective and guiding presence of Allah in life's journey. The strong historical, cultural, and spiritual connection to the original Badr Battle only amplifies the significance of the name Badran.
